fields.Name: totara

Configuration.AuthFlowNote: Totara Web Services (a Moodle-inherited layer) authenticates via a single opaque 'wstoken' -- a per-user Web Service token -- passed as a REQUEST PARAMETER (urlencoded BODY param on POST, or query-string param on GET), NEVER as an Authorization header, Basic credential, or OAuth2 bearer token. Confirmed directly from the operator-provided Postman collection's sole example request: POST {{base_url}}/webservice/rest/server.php?wsfunction=core_course_get_categories&moodlewsrestformat=json, with wstoken={{wstoken}} as a 'urlencoded' BODY parameter and auth.type='noauth' at the request level (the token itself IS the auth -- there is no separate auth scheme layered on top). Modeled as 'api-key' (a long-lived, non-expiring token credential) since it is neither OAuth2, Basic, nor header-based.
Configuration.AuthHeaderPattern: N/A -- no Authorization header is used. wstoken is injected as a request PARAMETER: POST {base_url}/webservice/rest/server.php?wsfunction=<fn>&moodlewsrestformat=json with a urlencoded body parameter wstoken=<token> (also accepted as an additional query-string parameter per the same protocol). The credential VALUE itself is never stored in this metadata file -- see Integration.CredentialTypeID (identity-establisher) and the per-connection CompanyIntegration.Configuration at connection time.
Configuration.TokenRefreshStrategyNote: N/A -- wstoken is a long-lived, non-expiring per-user Web Service token (an admin-issued credential, not an OAuth2 access token with a short TTL). No token-refresh/re-mint flow is documented anywhere in the 581-function surface audited for this build; the credential is revoked/re-issued by a site admin out-of-band, not refreshed by the connector.

RPCTransportModel.mechanism: Single-endpoint RPC-by-query-param dispatch (Moodle Web Services REST-RPC) -- NOT resource-path REST and NOT OpenAPI/GraphQL. Every one of the vendor doc's 581 documented operations (this connector models 28 as coverable Integration Objects) shares the IDENTICAL HTTP path and method; the operation identity lives entirely in the wsfunction= parameter value (e.g. wsfunction=core_course_get_courses).
RPCTransportModel.httpMethodNote: Both GET and POST are accepted by the underlying Moodle-WS endpoint in general, but the operator-provided Postman example and every one of the ACR doc's per-function 'REST (POST parameters)' blocks (581/581) demonstrate the POST shape -- the connector should follow POST consistently (also avoids URL-length limits on write operations with large bracket-array bodies -- see writeBodyEncoding).
RPCTransportModel.dispatchParamNote: The per-object dispatch value (which wsfunction a given Integration Object's read/write maps to) is set on that IntegrationObject's own row (APIPath at the IO level is this same shared path; DefaultQueryParams/Configuration on the IO records the specific wsfunction) by ioiof-extractor -- NOT recorded here. This Integration-level Configuration block documents the MECHANISM only, never a specific object's function name.

requiredParams.wsfunction: the operation selector (set per-IO, per-operation by ioiof-extractor)
requiredParams.moodlewsrestformat: 'json' -- REQUIRED on every call to force JSON responses (the same endpoint can otherwise return legacy XML-RPC/REST-XML rendering).
requiredParams.wstoken: the per-user Web Service token -- injected from the connector's resolved credential at request time, NEVER stored in this metadata file.

RPCTransportModel.writeBodyEncoding: Write operations (create/update/delete) use Moodle's bracket-notation urlencoded ARRAY body params (e.g. users[0][username]=..., users[0][customfields][0][value]=...), NOT a JSON body. Directly confirmed from core_user_create_users' own 'REST (POST parameters)' block in the ACR doc (users[0][createpassword]=int, users[0][username]=string, ... continuing through 30+ bracketed fields for a single array element) -- this exact bracket pattern ('[0][') recurs 625 times across the document, confirming it is the pervasive vendor-wide write encoding, not a one-off. This is a genuine per-operation override of the standard flat/wrapped JSON CreateBodyShape taxonomy; affected IOs should record CreateBodyShape/UpdateBodyShape='literal' with the override implemented in code per connector-code-conventions.md.
RPCTransportModel.citation: Transport/dispatch mechanism (wsfunction/moodlewsrestformat/wstoken, base_url placeholder, POST/urlencoded shape): sources/totara-rest-api.postman_collection.json (local, Tier 1, protocol-proof example request). Bracket-array write encoding: sources/totara-webservices-api-documentation.html (local, Tier 1, core_user_create_users REST (POST parameters) block).

Configuration.APIBaseURLNote: Totara/Moodle is self-hosted or vendor-hosted PER TENANT -- there is no shared totara.com API host. Every customer's site has its own base_url (its own domain), confirmed genuinely tenant-agnostic by the Postman collection's own empty {{base_url}} collection variable (never populated with a real host in the operator-provided artifact). The connector reads the tenant's site base_url from the per-connection CompanyIntegration config (NOT baked into this vendor-wide metadata file) and appends the fixed /webservice/rest/server.php suffix to build every request URL. Integration.NavigationBaseURL (root field) is set to this same template placeholder for the identical reason -- there is no vendor-wide real host to record. NEVER cite or bake in the operator-provided tenant instance live host anywhere in this connector's code or metadata.

universalPK.note: A strong, vendor-wide Moodle convention: every coverable object's per-record response object declares 'id' as its OWN first named field (even when the record is nested inside an envelope wrapper key, e.g. {users:[{id,...}]} or {items:[{id,...}]}). Directly re-verified for 5 of the 28 coverable anchors in this pass (core_course_get_courses -> id int //course id; core_user_get_users -> users[].id int //ID of the user; core_cohort_get_cohorts -> id int //ID of the cohort; hierarchy_organisation_index -> items[].id int //org id; core_group_get_groups -> id int //group record id), consistent with SOURCE_STUDY.md's independent audit of all 28 (25/28 confirmed typed with 'id' as the per-record identifier; the remaining 3 totara_competency_* leaves have NO typed response in this source at all -- see DiscoveryMechanism/known-gaps note below, their PK cannot be assumed 'id' from this hint and must be resolved via runtime DiscoverFields/live probe).

DiscoveryMechanism.description: Returns site info, user info, and a 'functions' list (each entry: {name, version}) of the Web Service functions ENABLED FOR THE CALLING TOKEN. Directly confirmed present in the ACR doc with exactly this response shape. This is the connector's runtime DiscoverObjects signal (per-tenant Discovered rows), not a vendor-wide Declared catalog.
DiscoveryMechanism.enumeratesFunctionsNotFieldsNote: core_webservice_get_site_info enumerates FUNCTION NAMES + versions the token can call -- it does not describe field-level response schema for those functions, so it cannot itself populate IntegrationObjectField rows.
DiscoveryMechanism.DiscoveryIsAuthoritativeRationale: core_webservice_get_site_info is TOKEN-SCOPED -- a different admin/service-account token on the SAME site could see a different enabled-function set (role/capability-gated), so it is not a complete-gamut describe of the site's total capability. Per connector-code-conventions.md, absence of a function in one token's enumerated list must NOT trigger deactivation of a Declared IO/IOF -- a role/permission change (not a schema change) could explain the absence. DiscoveryIsAuthoritative is left false so a comprehensive-refresh never wrongly deactivates Declared metadata based on one token's visible slice.

ErrorResponseShape.envelope: { exception: string, errorcode: string, message: string, debuginfo: string }
ErrorResponseShape.note: Moodle/Totara Web Services signal an error via a body ENVELOPE, not a non-2xx HTTP status. Directly confirmed vendor-wide: every one of the 581 documented functions (581/581, exact match) carries an identical 'Error message' block in the ACR doc showing the XML-RPC/REST-XML rendering: <EXCEPTION class="invalid_parameter_exception"><MESSAGE>Invalid parameter value detected</MESSAGE><DEBUGINFO></DEBUGINFO></EXCEPTION>. The JSON-format field names above (exception/errorcode/message/debuginfo) are the well-established Moodle JSON-serialization equivalent of this same exception object (moodlewsrestformat=json is required per RPCTransportModel) -- this exact JSON rendering is NOT literally printed anywhere in this doc source (only the XML rendering is shown), so this specific field-naming is ImpliedFromExample, not a doc-literal ExplicitStatement; NormalizeResponse should still treat the presence of this envelope shape as an error regardless of the (200) HTTP status, and a live/sandbox probe should confirm the exact JSON key casing before hard-coding a parser against it.
ErrorResponseShape.commonErrorClassesNote: invalid_parameter_exception is the one directly observed in this source (all 581 Error-message blocks use this same class in their worked example). webservice_access_exception / moodle_exception are the other standard Moodle Web Services exception classes for auth/permission failures and general application errors respectively -- well-established Moodle-core behavior, not directly rendered as a worked example in this particular doc source (cross-referenced only, not doc-literal here).

offsetMechanism.note: Many collection-read wsfunctions accept limitfrom (0-based row offset, 'sql limit from') + a page-size param as Arguments -- a classic OFFSET pagination shape. Directly confirmed two DISTINCT param-name variants coexist in this vendor's surface: 'limitnum' (e.g. Default to "0") on some functions, and 'limitnumber' ('maximum number of returned users') on others (e.g. core_enrol_get_enrolled_users-family functions) -- 25 limitfrom occurrences paired with 21 limitnum + 4 limitnumber occurrences, confirming both spellings are real and per-function, not a single canonical pair. PaginationType='Offset' (deployed enum {None,Cursor,Offset,PageNumber}) is set at the IntegrationObject level ONLY for functions whose own Arguments block documents one of these param pairs -- never assumed vendor-wide.

noPaginationMechanism.note: A substantial share of the 28 coverable functions return the FULL set unpaginated (no limitfrom/limitnum(ber) in their Arguments block at all) -- PaginationType='None' for those IOs. This is a genuine per-function split, not a uniform vendor convention; ioiof-extractor determines PaginationType per-IO from each function's own documented Arguments, never inherited from this Configuration block.

PaginationDefaults.note: No Cursor or PageNumber pagination form was found anywhere in the 581-function surface -- Totara/Moodle WS pagination is exclusively the limitfrom/limitnum(ber) OFFSET shape where present, and unpaginated (None) otherwise. The deployed PaginationType enum's Cursor/PageNumber values are simply unused by this vendor.

IncrementalSyncCapability.scope: per-function, PARTIAL -- a minority of the 28 coverable leaves document an incremental signal

mechanisms.note: Documented 'Check if there are updates on the course...since a certain time' -- returns an updated-items list, a delta/check signal layered on top of core_course_get_contents rather than a full re-fetch.
Companion check_updates function alongside get_updates_since; supports incremental change-detection at the course level.

A subset of typed Response blocks include a timemodified field on individual records (e.g. some course/user rows), which can serve as a content-hash/keyset fallback signal even where no dedicated incremental wsfunction exists for that object -- confirmed present on a subset of objects by direct inspection during this build, not a vendor-wide guarantee.

IncrementalSyncCapability.note: Where neither a dedicated incremental wsfunction nor a timemodified-shaped field is documented for a given object, the connector falls back to content-hash or keyset(id) sync per connector-code-conventions.md's sync-efficiency contract -- never assumed watermark support. Per-IO SupportsIncrementalSync + IncrementalWatermarkField are ioiof-extractor's determination, object by object.

WriteCapability.scope: Full CRUD via dedicated write wsfunctions on most coverable objects -- Courses, Users, Cohorts (+ members), Groups (+ members), Groupings, Enrolment (enrol/unenrol), Notes, Calendar Events, Contacts/Blocked Users (block/unblock) all have documented create/update/delete/add/remove functions in the ACR doc.
WriteCapability.bodyEncoding: Moodle bracket-notation urlencoded ARRAY params -- see RPCTransportModel.writeBodyEncoding. Recorded as CreateBodyShape/UpdateBodyShape='literal' on affected IOs (ioiof-extractor's determination), with the override implemented in code per connector-code-conventions.md.
WriteCapability.note: Per-object write function names, paths (all sharing the shared APIPath), and required Arguments are ioiof-extractor's determination -- this Integration-level Configuration records only the vendor-wide write MECHANISM (transport, body encoding), never a specific object's function name or body shape.

Configuration.ConcurrencyControlNote: No ETag / If-Match / If-Unmodified-Since header mechanism could apply to this transport at all (every request parameter -- including wstoken -- is a body/query PARAMETER, not an HTTP header; see RPCTransportModel), and no explicit version/revision argument is documented on any write operation's Arguments block anywhere in the 581-function surface audited for this build. A subset of objects carry a read-side timemodified field (see IncrementalSyncCapability) but no write operation accepts a matching 'expected last-modified' parameter to guard against a lost update. Conflict handling for any future bidirectional EntityMap must default to snapshot-3-way -- never MostRecent (no reliable revision/timestamp-of-write signal exists to arbitrate).
Configuration.DeleteSemanticsNote: Every documented delete-shaped wsfunction on the coverable objects (core_course_delete_courses, core_user_delete_users, core_cohort_delete_cohorts, core_group_delete_groups/groupings, core_notes_delete_notes, core_calendar_delete_calendar_events, delete_cohort_members, delete_group_members) is described as a straightforward removal, with no accompanying soft-delete/archive/status flag or recovery/undelete function documented in this source. No 'suspended'/'archived'/'deleted' flag field appears in any of the 28 coverable objects' typed Response blocks audited for this build. Treated as hard delete -- provable-only; no evidence of a tombstone mechanism was found. A live/sandbox probe should re-confirm before any delete write-back is enabled (see BidirectionalPreconditions).
Configuration.DefaultSyncDirectionNote: Read-only default for every object per connector-code-conventions.md's client-data-safety discipline, regardless of the substantial documented write surface. Bidirectional sync requires sandbox validation first -- see BidirectionalPreconditions.
Configuration.DefaultConflictResolutionReason: ConcurrencyControl=none vendor-wide (no ETag/If-Match/version-argument documented on any write operation in this Tier-1 source, and the transport has no HTTP-header channel to carry one anyway) rules out MostRecent as a safe default -- MostRecent needs a reliable revision/timestamp-of-write signal to arbitrate conflicts, which this API does not expose anywhere. DestWins is the conservative default if/when any write-capable object is later enabled for bidirectional sync: on pull, the MJ destination reflects the Totara site's own source-of-truth state, avoiding silent conflict-loss until a real concurrency signal is found.
BidirectionalPreconditions: Confirm via a live/sandbox Totara site + real wstoken that the bracket-notation write body encoding (RPCTransportModel.writeBodyEncoding) round-trips correctly for each write-capable object before enabling any push/create/update/delete path -- this build's evidence is doc-derived (ACR page's per-function Arguments blocks), never live-confirmed.

Confirm no soft-delete/archive/recovery mechanism exists on a live site before treating a write-back delete as safe -- current evidence (no tombstone/status field documented on any of the 28 coverable objects, no undelete function found) implies delete is hard and unrecoverable, but this is doc-derived, not live-verified.

Confirm no concurrency/version signal exists on a live write call (current evidence: none found, and the transport has no header channel) before ever recommending MostRecent conflict resolution -- DestWins/snapshot-3-way only until proven otherwise.
Confirm the exact JSON field names of the error envelope (ErrorResponseShape) against a live moodlewsrestformat=json response -- this build only directly observed the XML rendering in the source doc.

RealityProbe (S7, read-only) can verify write-surface EXISTENCE (401/403 reachability, OPTIONS) without ever performing a live mutation; a genuine live create/update/delete round-trip against a sandbox tenant remains a precondition for turning bidirectional ON for any specific object.
Configuration.WebhooksNote: No webhook / push-notification / event-subscription mechanism is documented anywhere in the ACR doc's 581 function blocks (zero 'webhook' occurrences in the source, confirmed by direct search) or in the cross-referenced official Totara developer docs consulted during this build. The one 'PUSH Notifications' hit in the source (core_user_add_user_device, 'Store mobile user devices information for PUSH Notifications') is mobile-APP push-notification device registration, not an outbound integration webhook -- already recorded as an excluded no-read-capability function, not a webhooks capability. Totara/Moodle Web Services (this legacy surface) is a pure pull/RPC surface.
Configuration.BulkOperationsNote: No SEPARATE bulk/batch endpoint path exists (contrast HubSpot's shared '/batch/*' path or Zendesk's per-resource '_many' suffix) -- bulk write is native to the NORMAL write call shape instead: every documented create/update/delete wsfunction for the coverable objects accepts an ARRAY of the target resource in the SAME single call (e.g. core_user_create_users takes a users[] array -- directly confirmed via the users[0][...] bracket-notation Arguments; core_cohort_delete_cohorts takes a cohortids[] array). There is no distinct bulk-READ endpoint beyond each list function's own already-bulk (list-returning) shape.
Configuration.APIVersioningNote: No URL-path, header, or Accept-header API version marker was found anywhere in the ACR doc or the Postman collection -- the endpoint path (/webservice/rest/server.php) and every wsfunction name are unversioned. Totara/Moodle manage behavior changes across releases via function deprecation/addition (e.g. newer get_X_by_field forms alongside older get_X forms) rather than a version parameter the connector must set.
Configuration.CustomObjectMarkerPatternNote: No vendor-imposed custom-object naming convention was found in this source. Totara's extensibility surface here is entirely at the PLUGIN level (a site installs a plugin, which registers its own wsfunction prefix -- e.g. this audited site's local_intellicart_*/local_intelliboard_*/local_intellidata_*/block_products_*/profilefield_vendor_*/format_tiles_*, see OutOfScopeObjectFamilies) rather than a custom-object marker WITHIN a fixed object's own data (contrast HubSpot's p_<accountID>_<name> convention). A different tenant's Web Services catalog would show a different plugin-prefix set entirely -- there is no single vendor-wide marker to record.
Configuration.CustomFieldMarkerPatternNote: No documented naming convention marks a custom field WITHIN a coverable object's typed Response schema in this source (e.g. a Moodle/Totara custom user profile field is not distinguishable from a built-in field by a naming prefix in the core_user_get_users response). Per-tenant custom fields flow through the framework's runtime custom-column capture path (full-record pass-through -> __mj_integration_CustomOverflow -> promotion), never a doc-derived static marker.

Configuration.OutOfScopeSummaryNote: 581 total documented wsfunctions on the operator-provided ACR site instance; 28 are the in-scope coverable Moodle-core + Totara-core LMS object graph (this connector's TaxonomyLeaves), 88 are informational CRUD/detail support for those 28, and the 465 functions enumerated above (175 tenant-installed-plugin + 168 activity-internal + 122 no-read-capability/ui-support-internal/test-scaffolding across 17 named families) are recorded out-of-scope WITH a reason each so a future connector iteration can expand without re-discovering. Ledger closes exactly: 28+88+175+168+122=581. See SOURCES.json.scopeDecision + SOURCE_STUDY.md for the full ledger and per-family evidence (this Configuration block passes that ledger through, it does not re-derive it -- re-derivation is source-auditor/ioiof-extractor's responsibility).
Configuration.LegacySurfaceStatusNote: Totara's own current developer documentation (totara.atlassian.net/wiki/display/DEV/Available+APIs) marks this ENTIRE Web Services surface (wsfunction/wstoken/server.php) 'not recommended' and 'deprecated', with the External GraphQL API (Totara 17+) named as the vendor's current recommended integration surface. This connector targets the still-functional legacy surface per the operator-provided/rooted sources; a future GraphQL-based connector iteration is a natural, additive follow-up (see SOURCE_STUDY.md 'Known gaps'), not a retrofit of this one.

Configuration.ObjectDispatchHintsNote: NON-AUTHORITATIVE Integration-level cross-reference for a subset of the 28 coverable objects (this batch: 22 named objects handed off as gap-fill work), independently extracted + structurally verified by scripts/extract-object-dispatch-hints.mjs directly against sources/totara-webservices-api-documentation.html (candidate wsfunction hypothesized from Moodle/Totara naming convention, then confirmed present with a matching Response 'General structure'/empty-untyped shape) and sources/totara-rest-api.postman_collection.json (protocol confirmation: POST, wsfunction=/moodlewsrestformat=json query params). Exists because this vendor's RPC-by-query-param protocol has NO canonical REST-path field to carry per-object identity (every object shares the identical /webservice/rest/server.php path -- see RPCTransportModel) -- this key lets a code-builder resolve which wsfunction backs a given object name from the Integration record alone. THE CANONICAL, AUTHORITATIVE assignment is each object's own MJ: Integration Object row (Configuration.wsfunction, set by ioiof-extractor) -- if this cross-reference and an IO row's own Configuration.wsfunction ever disagree, the IO row wins. requiredScopeArgs/paginationParams here are informational extraction hints only, not a substitute for the IO/IOF's own IsRequired/PaginationType/SupportsPagination fields.

Configuration.incrementalNote: Gap-7 decision (documented, not silently dropped): a companion delta function is documented at Integration.Configuration.IncrementalSyncCapability (core_course_get_updates_since / core_course_check_updates, appliesTo Courses/Course Contents) but it is NOT a watermark param on the LIST function (core_course_get_courses / core_course_get_contents) — it returns an updated-item-id LIST that requires a second re-fetch of changed rows. Flipping SupportsIncrementalSync=true + IncrementalWatermarkField here would fabricate a watermark on a list endpoint that has none. Configuration.idWindowScanRationale: core_user_get_users declares NO pagination params and the vendor docs state it 'could [be] very slow or timeout' without narrow criteria (and that the % wildcard 'may be considerably slower'). The defaultArgs email=% bulk list is therefore a documented anti-pattern: against a real-sized site it never returns inside the engine's FetchChangesMs budget and the object syncs ZERO rows behind a green run (observed live: 3x 30s timeouts, 0 users). Reads route through the bounded id-window scan below — an indexed PK lookup via the documented bulk reader — instead. defaultArgs is retained only as the legacy fallback if idWindowScan is removed. The window values below are the ones PROVEN against a live production site, not a guess: 25 ids per window x 2 windows per call reads 50 users in ~2.5s, an order of magnitude inside the 30s kill even when a window has to be bisected to isolate an unreadable id (25 -> 12 -> 6 -> 3 -> 2 -> 1 is 5 splits, under the default maxBisectSplitsPerCall of 8). Wider windows were tried first and failed live: 200 x 5 overran the budget and was killed with 0 records, and a 200-wide window containing one unreadable id could not finish its bisection inside the budget at all. maxConsecutiveEmptyWindows 40 tolerates a 1000-id gap of deleted users before the scan concludes it is past the end.
